title: Recording a dialect
bodyMd: A linguist records both older and younger speakers of a local dialect. Younger speakers use some new forms, which a commentator calls corruption. The linguist notes that earlier records also contain variation and argues that describing change differs from judging speakers. The archive keeps dates and speaker ages so future researchers can trace patterns rather than treat every recording as timeless.
